Assessment incorporating Financial Stability Report insights:
- Policy stance: The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continued balance sheet runoff, maintaining a restrictive stance until there is greater confidence inflation is moving sustainably to 2%. Implementation via the floor system remains in place (IORB at 5.4%, ON RRP at 5.3%, standing repo at 5.5%, and QT caps of $25B Treasuries and $35B agency MBS reinvested into Treasuries), supporting effective control of short rates.
- Macro tone vs risks: The statement acknowledges “modest further progress” on inflation and a better balance of risks, but the FSR context tempers this. Vulnerabilities include:
  • Funding risks in money market funds and broader short-term funding markets. 
  • Treasury market sensitivity to inflation, output growth, and the supply of Treasuries, alongside episodes of higher term premia and potential market liquidity strains. 
  • Weakness in economic activity could compound strains in real estate—particularly commercial real estate—as higher rates persist. 
  • Tight financial conditions can weigh on some households and businesses, with nonbank vulnerabilities remaining a watchpoint.
- Read-through: Overall tone is slightly positive on macro progress but offset by financial-stability risks highlighted in the FSR. This supports a cautious, anti-inflation posture without signaling imminent cuts and argues for a marginally less positive sentiment than a policy-only read.
